# USB Full-Speed Non-Buffered IN Protocol Engine

## 1. Overview

This module handles USB 2.0 Full-Speed IN transactions for a device. It watches incoming USB packets, recognizes IN and SETUP tokens addressed to the device, selects the appropriate response, streams payload data from the endpoint logic, and closes the transaction after a host handshake or timeout.

The module does not buffer USB packet payloads. It must be able to transfer payload bytes through to the transmit side as they are consumed, one byte at a time.

## 2. Token Recognition and Filtering

The module shall evaluate completed packets presented to it by the receive path. A packet shall be considered only if it ends with a valid indication.

The module shall recognize a token as relevant only when:

- its PID type is a token PID,
- its PID is either IN or SETUP, and
- its address field matches the configured USB device address.

All other packets and all packets addressed to other devices shall be ignored, except that ACK and NAK handshakes are monitored while waiting for a response to a transmitted data packet.

When a relevant IN token is received, the module shall:

- update its current endpoint context to the endpoint number carried by the token;
- indicate to the endpoint logic that a new IN request has been received;
- capture whether the endpoint has data available at that time.

A transaction-start indication shall be generated only when the requested endpoint is implemented and enabled. If the endpoint is not implemented or not enabled, the module shall send no response for that IN token.

## 3. Response Selection

For a relevant IN token addressed to an implemented and enabled endpoint, the module shall select a response in the following priority order:

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| Endpoint is isochronous | Send a DATA0 packet. If no data was captured, send a zero-length DATA0 packet. |
| Endpoint is stalled | Send a STALL handshake. |
| Data was captured as available | Send a DATA0 or DATA1 packet, according to the endpoint data toggle. |
| No data available | Send a NAK handshake. |

The data-availability indication used for response selection is captured when the IN token is received. A data-available flag that changes later must not affect the response to the current IN token.

IN tokens to unsupported or disabled endpoints shall not produce any response.

## 4. Data Packet Transmission

For a DATA packet response, the module shall start a transmit packet with the selected DATA PID. It shall then make the endpoint payload available to the transmit path in order, starting at offset zero.

As each byte is consumed by the transmit path, the module shall:

- advance the current payload offset;
- indicate to the endpoint logic that the byte was consumed so the next byte can be supplied.

The module shall continue transmitting payload bytes until the endpoint indicates that no more data remains or until the final byte has been consumed. The packet shall end according to the amount of data supplied by the endpoint.

Because the module has no packet storage, the endpoint logic must be able to provide payload bytes as they are requested.

## 5. Handshake and Transaction Completion

After a non-isochronous DATA packet has been transmitted, the module shall wait for the host response. The wait time shall be consistent with the USB 2.0 handshake timeout window, nominally 17 bit times.

The following behaviors shall apply while waiting:

- A valid ACK shall complete the transaction successfully.
- A valid NAK shall be treated as a failed transaction and shall be reported as a NAK event.
- A new valid IN token received before the ACK shall cause the previous transaction to be rolled back. If the endpoint for the new token is implemented and enabled, the module shall start a new IN transaction for that token.
- Any other packet received before the ACK shall cause the transaction to be rolled back and shall be reported as a timeout event.
- If no response arrives within the timeout window, the transaction shall be rolled back and reported as a timeout event.

Isochronous data transactions shall not wait for a handshake after the DATA0 packet is transmitted.

The module shall indicate successful completion only for:

- a non-isochronous data packet that receives ACK;
- an isochronous data packet when the captured data-available flag was set.

The module shall indicate rollback for any non-isochronous data transaction that ends without receiving ACK.

NAK and STALL responses sent immediately in reply to an IN token do not produce either a completion indication or a rollback indication.

## 6. Data Toggle Management

The module shall maintain one data toggle bit for each IN endpoint.

The toggle behavior shall be as follows:

- A valid SETUP token addressed to an implemented and enabled endpoint shall set that endpoint’s data toggle to 1.
- A successful ACK for a non-isochronous IN data packet shall invert the data toggle of the endpoint that sent the packet.
- Isochronous transactions shall not change data toggle state.
- A link reset shall clear all data toggle bits.
- A module reset shall clear all data toggle bits.

Software shall be able to read the current data toggle state and update selected endpoint bits. When a software update is presented, the selected bits shall take the supplied values, and unselected bits shall remain unchanged.

## 7. Link Reset and Link Inactivity

When the USB link is reset, the module shall:

- abandon any transaction in progress;
- return to an idle condition;
- clear all data toggle state;
- suppress any in-progress completion or rollback indication.

When the link is deactivated but not reset, the module shall abandon any transaction in progress and ignore further received packets. Link deactivation alone shall not necessarily clear data toggle state.

## 8. Event Indications

The module shall generate event indications for the following conditions:

- **Timeout**: a non-isochronous IN data packet did not receive an ACK. This includes an absent host response, an unexpected packet in the handshake window, or a new IN token arriving before the ACK.
- **NAK after data**: the host returned a NAK handshake after a non-isochronous IN data packet.
- **No data**: a relevant IN token addressed an implemented endpoint whose data-available flag was false at the time the token was received. This includes supported endpoints that are not currently enabled or configured. Endpoint numbers outside the implemented endpoint range shall not produce this event.
